name: Wearables & Movement Analytics
goal: Job-ready for a Whoop/Fitbit/Oura-style data-science role by Dec 2026 graduation

strategy.notes: Breadth-first: introduce new unlocked concepts broadly rather than drilling depth. Prereq gate lowered to 0.4 so downstream concepts unlock after ~two passes. Do NOT re-teach general ML, CNNs, prob/stat, or time-series basics; the learner has these from CMSE 381/404, STT 380, PHY/MTH coursework. Teach only the wearables-specific layer.

practical_artifacts.label: PAMAP2 hardware setup (from dataset readme)
practical_artifacts.value: 3 Colibri wireless IMUs @ 100 Hz (wrist/dominant arm, chest, dominant-side ankle); HR monitor BM-CS5SR @ ~9 Hz. IMU channels per unit: temperature, 3D accel (+/-16g and +/-6g), 3D gyro (rad/s), 3D magnetometer (uT), orientation.
practical_artifacts.note: Real column layout: col1 timestamp(s), col2 activityID, col3 heart rate(bpm), col4-20 IMU hand, col21-37 IMU chest, col38-54 IMU ankle.

practical_artifacts.label: UCI HAR sensor setup
practical_artifacts.value: Samsung Galaxy S II worn on the waist; embedded accelerometer + gyroscope; 3-axial linear acceleration and 3-axial angular velocity captured at 50 Hz.

practical_artifacts.label: UCI HAR windowing scheme
practical_artifacts.value: Signals sampled in fixed-width sliding windows of 2.56 sec with 50% overlap = 128 readings/window at 50 Hz. Acceleration separated into body + gravity via Butterworth low-pass with 0.3 Hz cutoff.

practical_artifacts.label: PAMAP2 mixed sampling rates + missingness
practical_artifacts.value: IMU data every 0.01s (100 Hz); HR monitor only ~9 Hz, so missing HR rows are filled with NaN. Real IMU frequencies were 99.63/99.89/99.65 Hz (hand/chest/ankle), not exactly 100.

practical_artifacts.label: Devices compared in the ECG-vs-PPG study
practical_artifacts.value: PPG-based sensor: Polar OH1 (optical, forearm). ECG reference: Polar H10 (chest strap). PPG estimates pulse from blood-volume changes; motion artifacts degrade it.

practical_artifacts.label: HRV metrics from the 1996 ESC/NASPE Task Force standard
practical_artifacts.value: Time-domain: SDNN (SD of NN intervals), RMSSD (root mean square of successive differences). Frequency-domain bands: ULF, VLF, LF (0.04-0.15 Hz), HF (0.15-0.4 Hz). LF/HF ratio used as an autonomic-balance proxy.
practical_artifacts.note: The analysis operates on the RR/NN interval tachogram (intervals between consecutive heartbeats), not the raw HR value.

practical_artifacts.label: Reliability results (Polar OH1 PPG vs Polar H10 ECG, n=31 adults)
practical_artifacts.value: Supine: RMSSD ICC=0.955, SDNN ICC=0.980 (excellent). Seated: RMSSD ICC=0.834, SDNN ICC=0.921 (good). Mean bias -2.1 ms to -8.1 ms. Agreement worse in older participants and females; posture change supine->seated dropped reliability.
practical_artifacts.note: PPG yields pulse-rate variability (PRV), a surrogate for true ECG-derived HRV, not an identical measurement.

practical_artifacts.label: Wearable sleep staging landscape (from the 2025 review)
practical_artifacts.value: Ground truth = polysomnography (PSG). Accelerometer-only (actigraphy) does sleep/wake well but struggles to separate stages; combining accelerometer + PPG enables out-of-lab multi-stage staging. Devices: wristbands, rings, headbands, camera-based.

practical_artifacts.label: Composite-score inputs (generic; avoid claiming any vendor's exact proprietary formula)
practical_artifacts.value: Recovery/readiness scores are composed from overnight HRV (often RMSSD-based), resting heart rate, respiratory rate, and sleep quantity/quality. Strain-type scores integrate heart-rate zones over the day. Exact weightings are proprietary and vendor-specific.

practical_artifacts.label: Lara & Labrador two-level HAR taxonomy
practical_artifacts.value: Axis 1 (learning approach): supervised vs semi-supervised. Axis 2 (response time): offline vs online. Also: external sensing (sensors in the environment) vs wearable sensing (sensors on the body).

practical_artifacts.label: UCI HAR 561-feature vector
practical_artifacts.value: From each 2.56s window, a 561-feature vector of time-domain and frequency-domain variables (mean, std, energy, entropy, FFT coefficients, etc.). Features normalized and bounded within [-1, 1]. See features_info.txt for the full list.

practical_artifacts.label: UCI HAR label set + models
practical_artifacts.value: 6 activity classes: WALKING, WALKING_UPSTAIRS, WALKING_DOWNSTAIRS, SITTING, STANDING, LAYING. Strong classical baselines on the 561-feature vector: Random Forest, SVM, k-NN. WISDM alternative: 36 subjects, 20 Hz accel, classes Walking/Jogging/Sitting/Standing/Upstairs/Downstairs.

practical_artifacts.label: Deep HAR on raw windows (PAMAP2)
practical_artifacts.value: Feed raw windowed sensor channels (no hand-crafted features) into 1D-CNN or LSTM. PAMAP2: 18 activities incl. lying, running, cycling, Nordic walking, rope jumping, vacuuming, ironing. Recommend the +/-16g accelerometer over +/-6g (the 6g one saturates during high-impact movement like running).

practical_artifacts.label: Movement-quality tasks beyond activity labels
practical_artifacts.value: Cadence (steps/min), stride/step symmetry, gait variability, fall detection, and posture. Clinical hooks named in the HAR survey: monitoring diabetes/obesity exercise routines, detecting abnormal activity in dementia, Parkinson's assessment. This is the kinesiology-moat concept.

practical_artifacts.label: Agreement methods for wearable validation
practical_artifacts.value: Intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) for reliability; Bland-Altman plots for mean bias + limits of agreement between a device and its reference. References: ECG (Polar H10) for HR/HRV, PSG for sleep. Accuracy is not one number: it varies by posture, age, and sex (see ECG-vs-PPG study).

practical_artifacts.label: Leakage from random window splitting
practical_artifacts.value: train_test_split(windows, test_size=0.3, shuffle=True)  # windows from the SAME subject land in train AND test
bugs: overlapping windows from one person leak across the split
inflated accuracy that collapses on new users
fix: split BY subject (leave-one-subject-out / GroupKFold on subject id)
practical_artifacts.note: UCI HAR ships a correct 70/30 SUBJECT-wise split (21 train subjects / 9 test); WISDM has 36 subjects for LOSO.

practical_artifacts.label: PAMAP2 data-quality gotchas
practical_artifacts.value: Missing values marked NaN (wireless dropout; HR sampled slower than IMU). activityID=0 = transient activity and must be discarded before analysis. ~10 hours collected, only ~8 hours labeled. Class imbalance across the 18 activities. Some subjects missing some activities.

practical_artifacts.label: Ingestion & inference placement
practical_artifacts.value: Stream: device -> BLE/companion app -> cloud ingestion -> feature store -> model. Trade-off: on-device/edge inference (low latency, battery + privacy) vs cloud (heavier models, retrainable). Ties to the learner's harness-engineering domain.

practical_artifacts.label: Industry/regulatory framing (Rajpurkar & Topol, Nature Medicine 2022)
practical_artifacts.value: FDA clearances for ML devices growing at an accelerating rate but mostly cleared on retrospective, single-institution, often-proprietary data. RCTs/prospective studies are what actually validate clinical impact. Reporting standards: STARD-AI, SPIRIT/CONSORT AI extensions. Consumer wearables mostly sit as wellness (non-diagnostic) unless specifically cleared.

practical_artifacts.label: Interview-ready capstone spec
practical_artifacts.value: On WISDM or PAMAP2: raw signal -> windowing -> features (or raw for deep model) -> classifier -> SUBJECT-WISE validation -> honest metrics with a confusion matrix -> a written result. Deliverable lives in sandbox/digital_health/scripts. The differentiator is subject-wise evaluation + a data-quality writeup, not raw accuracy.
